Thesis: 7shifts earns budget when applicant tracking; career site and job boards; core hris; payroll processing is the operating loop; walk when Hospitality-specialist — not a general retail/field WFM because it forces workarounds.

Best for: Restaurants and hospitality groups that want scheduling, punches, tips, and POS in one WFM; Operators comparing 7shifts as the hospitality default versus Homebase; Teams that will trial Pro for 14 days before Premium payroll (Restaurants and hospitality groups that want scheduling, punches, tips, and POS in one WFM).

sections.heading: 7shifts limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Hospitality-specialist — not a general retail/field WFM; Per-location pricing and employee caps force Pro/Premium as sites grow; Tip/task/auto-scheduler depth is Premium-gated because it forces process changes or add-ons around 7shifts when applicant tracking is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Comp (Free) until payroll processing (Comp (Free), Essentials, Pro, Premium) is mandatory; plan jumps to Essentials only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain payroll processing (Comp (Free), Essentials, Pro, Premium) at the expense of Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Comp (Free) · free · applicant tracking | Essentials | Pro.

Alternative context: unlike Homebase, 7shifts is preferable when Restaurants and hospitality groups that want scheduling, punches, tips, and POS in one WFM because applicant tracking plus payroll processing (Comp (Free), Essentials, Pro, Premium) match; prefer Homebase when Non-restaurant hourly businesses (Homebase / When I Work / Connecteam fit better) because the operating loops differ.
